A conv on edge 1 already supplies capacity to node 2, so a further 3x3 on edge 5 adds less.
A strong direct conv into node 3 already supplies capacity, so an extra 1x1 branch adds little.
The direct 3x3 path already supplies spatial capacity, so a conv at the head of the serial path is partly redundant.
Pooling on edge 0 blurs the multi-hop route, so the direct conv becomes the main source of sharp spatial features.
With the node 2 route to the output cut, a skip restores shallow information from node 1 into the output.
When the multi-hop route is pooled and loses detail, a direct 1x1 supplies full-resolution channel mixing.
Edge 1 feeds edge 5 in series, so a 3x3 upstream supplies spatial mixing the downstream 1x1 lacks.
Without a direct edge, the path through node 2 carries more of the output so a strong conv on edge 5 matters more.
With edge 0 cut, node 1 is empty and edge 1 is the only way to feed node 2, so its conv carries all the learned depth on that route.
